title: The 10 Best Car Lifts for Home Garages
subtitle: Portable, mid-rise, 2-post, and 4-post car lifts, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A car lift replaces jack stands and lets you work under the car in comfort. Amazon sells four kinds: portable low-rise frames ($950 to $1,500) that lift about 27 inches and store against a wall, mid-rise scissor lifts around 39 inches, and anchored 2-post and drive-on 4-post lifts ($2,050 to $3,300) that raise a car to standing height. We ranked 10 on star rating, review volume, and features (portable, standing-height lift, published load testing, 110V power, and a 3-year warranty).

avoid.name: EliteEdge 7,000 lb Portable Car Lift, Scissor Lift Jack with Safety Lock, 6.26 to 27 in.
avoid.flag: Can't agree on its own capacity
avoid.verdict: It's one of the cheapest two-frame portable lifts here, but the listing contradicts itself on the one number that keeps a car off your chest. The Albott costs about $350 more and gives one consistent rating.
reasons: The first bullet's heading says "5000LBS Capacity" and the same sentence says it "supports 7000 lbs capacity". On a lift you work under, a 2,000 lb disagreement isn't a typo you can shrug off.
The title gives the lift range as 6.26 to 27 in., while the bullets say the columns cover 11 to 27 in. and only the pads go down to 6.26 in.
It promises "zero wobbling for ultimate safety" with no load test, certification, or warranty term to back it up.

buyers_guide.a: Portable low-rise lifts (about 27 to 28 in.) need no installation and store on a wall, but you work lying on a creeper. Mid-rise scissor lifts (about 39 in.) let you sit on a stool. 2-post lifts raise the car to standing height and leave the wheels hanging for brake and suspension work, but they must be anchored in solid concrete. 4-post lifts are drive-on, double as parking storage, and don't need anchoring.

buyers_guide.q: How high does my ceiling need to be?
buyers_guide.a: For a portable or mid-rise lift, a normal 8 ft garage is fine. For standing-height work, add the lift's max height, the car's roof height, and a few inches of clearance. The APlusLift 4-post is 94 in. tall before it lifts anything, and overhead 2-posts need room for the top beam. Most people need 11 to 12 ft for a 2-post or 4-post.

buyers_guide.q: Can my garage floor take a 2-post lift?
buyers_guide.a: 2-post lifts bolt into the slab, and most makers call for at least 4 in. of 3,000 psi concrete with no cracks or expansion joints under the posts. If you don't know your slab, drill a test hole first. Portable and 4-post lifts sit on the floor and don't need anchoring.

The portable lifts and the APlusLift and KATOOL 4-posts here run on 110V. Many 2-post lifts, including the KATOOL 12,000 lb and the Motool LM1100S, need a 220V circuit, which may mean paying an electrician.

buyers_guide.q: How do I get it off the truck?
buyers_guide.a: Portable lifts ship by parcel or LTL to the curb. Full 2-post and 4-post lifts often weigh 1,000 to 1,800 lb crated, and several sellers here require you to unload with a forklift or tractor, or pick up at a freight terminal. APlusLift includes liftgate service on some models; check before you order.
